{"id": "20:13/q09", "question": "What inward effect does God's choice have on Moses or the chosen servant?", "turns_on": "Different accounts of what selection does inwardly: preparation, purification and effacement, or awakening after self-disclosure.", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q09/p1", "position": "The chosen servant is nurtured for revelation, loved, articulate and made steadfast.", "reasons": "Al-Sulamī reports al-Wāsiṭī: God's choice nurtures and selects the servant, makes God's servants love him, enables clear speech, and eases his affairs so he can stand before revelation."}, {"id": "20:13/q09/p2", "position": "Choice purifies Moses of illusion and effaces his self so that he belongs to God and acts through Him.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī says God's choice is made with knowledge of Moses and strips away what clouds clarity; he also reports Moses' annihilation after selection."}, {"id": "20:13/q09/p3", "position": "Choice follows the collapse of Moses' separate existence and awakening through true existence.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī reads 7:143–144 as Moses' mountain-like existence crumbling in annihilation, his stunned fall, and subsequent awakening; he calls this disclosure of attributes before Essence."}]}
{"id": "20:13/q10", "question": "Why does the command to listen follow the announcement of selection?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q10/p1", "position": "Selection gives the reason for listening: Moses must attend to the revelation of his new calling.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī says the fāʾ makes listening follow from selection. {"id": "20:13/q11", "question": "What does 'listen' ask Moses to do?", "turns_on": "Whether the command is explained chiefly as concentrated hearing or as obedient action flowing from it.", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q11/p1", "position": "Attend silently and intently to the revelation, ready to understand it.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Anbārī glosses listening as silence and attention. Wahb specifies still limbs, lowered gaze, attentive hearing, present mind and intent to understand and act. Al-Iṣlāḥī says attention focuses Moses for revelation. Al-Ālūsī says the command signals the greatness of the revelation and the need to prepare for it; he reports Wahb's account of still limbs, lowered gaze, focused hearing and present understanding. Ibn ʿĀshūr says istamiʿ can convey aṣghi, attentive listening."}, {"id": "20:13/q11/p2", "position": "Listen so as to carry out the revealed commands and avoid prohibitions.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī explicitly interprets listening as acting on God's commands and prohibitions; Wahb includes a resolve to act in proper listening, and al-Bursawī says Moses listens to revealed commands and prohibitions. Al-Ālūsī reports Wahb's inclusion of a resolve to act on what God loves in attentive listening."}]}
{"id": "20:13/q12", "question": "How did Moses physically listen at this moment?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q12/p1", "position": "He stood at or leaned on a stone, hands folded, chin lowered, dressed in wool.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmits Abū al-Faḍl al-Jawharī; Qurṭubī cites Ibn ʿAṭiyya's father citing al-Jawharī; Abū Ḥayyān repeats the account. {"id": "20:13/q13", "question": "What is Moses to listen to?", "turns_on": "Whether the phrase points specifically to the declaration immediately following or to the revelation and instructions more broadly.", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q13/p1", "position": "God's declaration of exclusive divinity and the command to worship Him in 20:14.", "reasons": "Muqātil calls it God's declaration of oneness; Ibn al-Jawzī quotes 'I am God; there is no god but Me, so worship Me'; Abū Ḥayyān likewise identifies God's declaration of exclusive divinity."}, {"id": "20:13/q13/p2", "position": "The revelation now being spoken to Moses, including its commands and prohibitions.", "reasons": "Yaḥyā, al-Baghawī and Ibn Kathīr identify the revelation being given now; al-Bursawī specifies commands and prohibitions, while al-Wāḥidī says listening includes acting on both. {"id": "20:13/q14", "question": "Does mā mean revealed content or the act of revelation?", "turns_on": "Whether mā is a relative pronoun or a verbal-noun particle.", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q14/p1", "position": "A relative pronoun: that which is revealed.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Bayḍāwī and al-Nasafī offer this as one sense; Abū Ḥayyān favors it as the natural meaning; al-Samīn identifies the relative-pronoun parsing. {"id": "20:13/q15", "question": "Which verb governs the lām phrase 'to what is revealed'?", "turns_on": "Whether the phrase is governed by the command to listen or by the verb of selection; the objection to technical dual government is the missing repeated pronoun.", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q15/p1", "position": "It attaches to 'listen'; the lām can function as an added preposition before its object.", "reasons": "Al-Bayḍāwī, al-Nasafī and al-Samīn offer this attachment; al-Samīn prefers it as apparent, as does Abū Ḥayyān. Al-Bursawī calls the lām added before the object, comparing radifa lakum in 27:72; al-Samīn also cites 27:72 for an extra lām. Abū Ḥayyān argues that assigning technical government to 'chose' violates the two-governor rule without a repeated pronoun; al-Samīn reports his expected form as fastamiʿ lahu limā yūḥā. Al-Ālūsī cites this objection but also reports a reply allowing alternative coordination. Ibn ʿĀshūr says the lām reinforces istamiʿ's link to its object; alternatively, taking istamiʿ in the sense of aṣghi explains the lām with attentive listening."}, {"id": "20:13/q15/p2", "position": "It can attach to 'I chose you': Moses was chosen for revelation and must listen to it.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Bayḍāwī and al-Nasafī allow the attachment; al-Samīn reports al-Zamakhsharī and others as describing tanāzuʿ, but clarifies they mean semantic suitability rather than shared technical government. Al-Ṭabrisī reports Abū ʿAlī's special parsing of the plural as wa-li-annā ikhtarnāka, making that prepositional phrase the object of 'listen.' Al-Ālūsī records a reply permitting either attachment by alternative coordination. Ibn ʿĀshūr offers the attachment to 'I chose you for revelation' and treats the intervening command as parenthetical."}]}

{"id": "20:13/q17", "question": "How does the call unfold across the following verses?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q17/p1", "position": "The passage first states Moses' prophethood, then develops his mission through the staff question and command to go to Pharaoh.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads the next eleven verses as containing both prophecy and mission; the mission begins with the staff question and ends with the order to approach Pharaoh, and 19:51 names Moses both prophet and messenger."}, {"id": "20:13/q17/p2", "position": "The call begins with kindly choice and ends with a severe warning, teaching that mercy precedes wrath and the servant lives between hope and fear.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī contrasts the opening choice in 20:13 with the closing warning in 20:16 and draws the lessons of mercy before wrath and hope alongside fear."}, {"id": "20:13/q17/p3", "position": "The address reasons from God's identity and oneness to worship and prayer, then the Hour and requital, warning against deniers, and the ruin that follows disobedience.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr traces how each command and prohibition in the address follows from the preceding point."}]}

{"id": "20:13/q22", "question": "How is the nearby command to establish prayer for remembrance understood?", "turns_on": "Whether remembrance is within prayer, its entry, or recall of a forgotten prayer.", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q22/p1", "position": "Remember God during prayer.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī reports Mujāhid's explanation."}, {"id": "20:13/q22/p2", "position": "Begin prayer by remembering God, since prayer is entered only through His remembrance.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī reports this as another interpretation."}, {"id": "20:13/q22/p3", "position": "Pray when one remembers a missed prayer.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī reports Ibrāhīm's interpretation and Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib's Prophetic report that whoever forgets a prayer should perform it on remembering."}]}
{"id": "20:13/q23", "question": "Does God's direct speech to Moses establish his superiority over Muhammad?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q23/p1", "position": "No; God addressed Muhammad directly on the Night Journey, unveiled and with a vision that Moses was not granted.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī argues from the direct address to Muhammad on the Night Journey while discussing God's speech to Moses; he mentions 4:164 and 17:1."}]}
{"id": "20:13/q24", "question": "What does the predication in 'I chose you' accomplish?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:13/q24/p1", "position": "It reinforces the surprising announcement of choice so Moses will not doubt it; it does not restrict the assertion.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr explains that verbal predication strengthens unexpected news without making it exclusive."}]}
{"id": "20:24/q01", "question": "What is Moses commanded to do by going to Pharaoh?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:24/q01/p1", "position": "Approach Pharaoh with God's signs, call him to worship God alone, warn him, and seek his reform.", "reasons": "Muqatil, al-Tha'labi, al-Baghawi, al-Baydawi, al-Razi, and al-Alusi explicitly make the mission a summons to worship; al-Wahidi's People of Meanings supply the call to affirm divine oneness as understood wording. {"id": "20:24/q03", "question": "How did Moses respond to the command to go?", "turns_on": "The reports differ over Moses' hesitation, its duration, and whether the prompting angel is identified; al-Alusi questions the seven-day account.", "positions": [{"id": "20:24/q03/p1", "position": "He accepted the difficult commission and sought the breadth of heart needed to face Pharaoh.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayri says Moses accepted an ordeal against his own wish after being honored by direct divine speech, despite knowing Pharaoh would not respond. {"id": "20:24/q13", "question": "What does Wahb's report add to the commission of Moses?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "20:24/q13/p1", "position": "God reassured Moses of protection, then ordered a gentle summons to worship and warning while showing forbearance to Pharaoh.", "reasons": "Al-Razi reports Wahb's charge to deliver the message, summon Pharaoh to worship, warn him, speak gently, and trust God's protection and knowledge; he gives no grading.
